title: Systems of equations and constraints
purpose: Solve simultaneous conditions, distinguish solution types, and translate a model into an auditable system.

lessons.title: Two-variable linear systems
lessons.objective: Solve a two-variable system and distinguish one solution, no solution, and infinitely many solutions.
lessons.coverage: Substitution, elimination, graphical intersections, parallel versus coincident lines, and verification in both original equations.
lessons.activity: Predict the number of intersections, solve algebraically, and compare with two lines whose numerical coefficients are also available in a table.
families: Construct and solve a unique-solution linear system
Classify dependent or inconsistent pairs and interpret the geometry
lessons.generatorRules: Generate from a known solution or explicit proportional rows. Use a separate constant perturbation for inconsistent cases; never infer uniqueness from a rounded graph.
lessons.commonError: Calling 0=0 a zero-valued solution, calling 0=5 an unknown solution, or checking only one equation.
lessons.feedback: Interpret the reduced statement and substitute into every original equation.
lessons.checkpoint: Substitution, elimination, solution-type classification, and verification.

lessons.title: Three-variable elimination
lessons.objective: Reduce a three-variable system to simpler equations and verify the resulting ordered triple or describe a dependent family.
lessons.coverage: Consistent variable order, eliminating the same variable from two pairs, back substitution, contradictions, and one-parameter solution descriptions.
lessons.activity: Choose elimination combinations and track which variables remain after each step, with a visible record of equivalent systems.
families: Solve a three-variable system constructed from a known rational triple
Interpret a dependent or inconsistent system after a supplied reduction
lessons.generatorRules: Use small coefficients and reviewed row combinations. Include unique, inconsistent, and one-free-variable cases; avoid accidental large fractions in introductory tasks.
lessons.commonError: Eliminating different variables and treating the resulting equations as a complete two-variable system or losing a minus sign in back substitution.
lessons.feedback: Align variables in columns and verify each newly formed equation from its parent equations.
lessons.checkpoint: An elimination step, back substitution, a dependent-family interpretation, and full-system verification.

lessons.title: Nonlinear intersections and feasible regions
lessons.objective: Find all solutions of a small nonlinear system and interpret whether points satisfy simultaneous inequalities.
lessons.coverage: Line/parabola and line/circle intersections, substitution to a quadratic, multiple intersections, boundary inclusion, and intersection of constraint regions.
lessons.activity: Predict intersection count, compute exact candidates, then test each pair in both equations or each inequality. Provide a text list of boundary and test-point conditions.
families: Solve a constructed line-quadratic system with zero, one, or two real intersections
Classify a point or boundary in a feasible region defined by two inequalities
lessons.generatorRules: Generate known intersection cases and explicitly state real coordinates. Do not grade a visually selected point without numeric coordinates and boundary rules.
lessons.commonError: Returning x-values without corresponding y-values, omitting one intersection, or taking the union of constraints instead of the intersection.
lessons.feedback: Substitute each complete ordered pair and evaluate every constraint separately.
lessons.checkpoint: Two nonlinear-intersection items, one boundary decision, and one feasible-point classification.

lessons.title: Formulating and auditing systems
lessons.objective: Define variables and units, translate two or three supplied relationships into a system, and assess whether its solution is meaningful.
lessons.coverage: Calibration coefficients, totals and balance equations, independent information, exact models versus noisy observations, and checking physically allowed signs and ranges.
lessons.activity: Select equations for a two-sensor calibration, solve for offsets or gains, and discover why repeating the same observation adds no independent information.
families: Translate a short context into a labeled system and solve it
Identify redundant, inconsistent, or insufficient measurements and explain the consequence
lessons.generatorRules: Supply every domain relationship. Use exact synthetic observations unless noise is explicitly being discussed; least-squares fitting is outside the required solution methods.
lessons.commonError: Treating any two equations as independent or accepting a mathematical solution outside the stated operating range.
lessons.feedback: Attach units to every term and compare equation independence before performing elimination.
lessons.checkpoint: Variable definitions, equation selection, solution, and contextual validation.

anchor.prompt: Solve 2*x+y=7 and x-y=2; contrast this with x+y=2 and 2*x+2*y=5.
anchor.answer: The first system has (x,y)=(3,1). The second is inconsistent because twice the first left-hand side would require 4, not 5, on the right.

moduleExit: Require explicit solution-type classification and verification in all original equations, including one contextual system.
